In 1993 gingen de Heilig Hartschool en d: In 1993 the Heilig Hart school and the Sint-Anna school merged into De Schrank. The Heilig Hart school began in 1861 as a public primary school; the girls' school belonged to the Sint-Anna convent of the Franciscan sisters from Heythuysen, here from 1910 to 1959.
Bezoekerscentrum van Nationaal Park De G: Visitor centre of De Groote Peel National Park
De hoofdingang van Nationaal Park De Gro: The main entrance to De Groote Peel National Park, once called Mijl op Zeven: information, a terrace and the start of the walks into the raised bog. De Groote Peel has been a national park since 1993.
Hier stond de lagere school van Ospeldij: This was the primary school of Ospeldijk, first the Heilige Geest school, later 't Kienhout. It closed in 2012 for lack of pupils; now it is a Thomashuis, a small care home.

Een celtic field: de sporen van een preh: A celtic field: the traces of a prehistoric field system, small square fields with low banks around them, laid out between the late Bronze Age and Roman times.
Het sportpark van RKSVO, de voetbalclub: The grounds of RKSVO, Ospel's football club, founded in 1948.

In 1893 begonnen boeren aan de Klaarstra: In 1893 farmers on the Klaarstraat started a small cooperative dairy, worked by hand, under the motto Unity is strength. When the Sint-Isidorus steam dairy took over in 1906, the little building became a chapel to Our Lady of Perpetual Help, blessed in 1907.

Langs de dijk van Meijel naar Ospel groe: Along the dyke from Meijel to Ospel a ribbon of farms grew, on land reclaimed from the Peel. In 1954 Ospeldijk became a parish village. The church of 1958 closed in 2007 and was demolished a year later; the tower was left standing. The school of 1952 closed in 2012.
Kinderen uit Kreijel gingen vanaf 1829 n: From 1829 children in Kreijel went to a primitive little school; in 1861 Ospel got a public primary school, later the Heilig Hart school. In 1910 Franciscan sisters from Heythuysen came with a convent and a girls' school, the Sint-Anna school. The last sister left in 1959 and the convent became a community centre. In 1993 the two schools merged into De Schrank.

Kort nadat Ospel in 1864 een eigen paroc: Soon after Ospel became a parish of its own in 1864, Pierre Cuypers designed this brick cruciform basilica; it was built in 1866 and 1867. In 1944 the tower was blown up and the vaults destroyed. In 1953 and 1954 a new tower went up, with an octagonal spire between four corner turrets.
Een beltmolen uit 1869, op een plek waar: A mound mill from 1869, built where no mill had stood before. It ground grain until 1948, was stripped of its sails in 1970 and bought by the municipality in 1972. Since its restoration in 1990, volunteers grind grain here again, with two pairs of millstones.
Negentien boeren en Breukers lieten deze: Nineteen farmers and Breukers had this mound mill built in 1840, each owning a twentieth share. Around 1900 it got a suction gas engine, so it could grind when there was no wind. By about 1970 it was in poor repair; it was restored in 1979. Its sails, from 1978, are 24.80 metres across.
In 1893 stond hier een coöperatief melkf: In 1893 a small cooperative dairy stood here, worked by hand, under the motto Unity is strength. When the steam dairy took over in 1906, the building was turned into a chapel, blessed in 1907. Inside, the wooden vault is painted blue.
Een beeldengroep van Albert Verschuuren: A group of statues by Albert Verschuuren in the churchyard, at the grave of Father H. Caris, who died in 1926. Christ stands in the middle; beside him kneel a woman with a child and a man. The plinth reads: Behold your king.
Een zuil van roestvrij staal bij het bez: A three-sided stainless steel column by the visitor centre, in memory of the aircrews who died in the Peel during the Second World War.
In 1864 werd Ospel een eigen parochie, e: In 1864 Ospel became a parish of its own, and a village where the hamlets around it came for church, school and shop. Pierre Cuypers, the architect of the Rijksmuseum, designed the church: a brick Gothic Revival cruciform basilica, built in 1866 and 1867.
In 1944 werd de kerktoren opgeblazen en: In 1944 the church tower was blown up and the rib vaults collapsed. They were partly restored in 1946 and 1947; in 1953 and 1954 a new tower went up, with an octagonal spire between four corner turrets and a hexagonal stair tower beside it. In 1956 a new Vermeulen organ followed.
Bij het graf van pastoor H. Caris, die i: At the grave of Father H. Caris, who died in 1926, stands a Sacred Heart group by Albert Verschuuren. A photo from 1935 shows it on a stepped platform, with a lantern at each end of the wall and on the plinth: Behold your king.
Negentien boeren en Breukers lieten in K: Nineteen farmers and Breukers had a mound mill built in Kreijel, each owning a twentieth share. Around 1900 it got a suction gas engine, so it could run when there was no wind. By about 1970 it was in poor repair; it was restored in 1979.
Het jonge dorp kreeg in 1869 een eigen k: In 1869 the young village got a corn mill of its own. De Korenbloem ground grain until 1948 and then fell into disrepair; in 1970 it lost its sails. The municipality bought it in 1972 and had it restored in 1990. Now volunteers grind grain here again.
De pastorie dateert uit 1864, het jaar w: The presbytery dates from 1864, the year Ospel became a parish of its own.
Vector of Memory herdenkt de Amerikaanse: Vector of Memory honours the US 7th Armored Division. On 27 October 1944 German troops retook Meijel and Ospel in a surprise attack; in early November the Americans took Ospel back, losing 54 dead and over 300 wounded. The memorial was unveiled on 26 May 2007.
Het bluesfestival Moulin Blues wordt sin: The Moulin Blues festival has been held in Ospel since 1986, over two days since 1995. B.B. King, Buddy Guy and Joe Bonamassa are among those who played. The grounds used to be on the Meijelsedijk; now they are at the Stenenbrug.
Een schans van 1,1 hectare met bastions: A 1.1 hectare redoubt with corner bastions and a moat, where people from the surrounding hamlets fled in troubled times. In 1821 it was sold at public auction with its moats; around 1840 the map called it Vervallen Schans, the ruined redoubt.
Op 27 oktober 1944 heroverden Duitse tro: On 27 October 1944 German troops retook Meijel and Ospel from the US 7th Armored Division in a surprise attack. In early November the Americans took Ospel back; the division lost 54 dead and over 300 wounded here. Since 2007 a memorial to the American liberators has stood on the Plattepeeldijk.
In 1937 werd gevraagd om een peelreserva: In 1937 a reserve was proposed on the border of Brabant and Limburg; in 1951 the state forestry service bought the first land. On the Limburg side the land was so fragmented that 875 hectares took over 500 deeds. The Mijl op Zeven visitor centre, a copy of a Peel farmhouse, opened in 1966.
Eeuwenlang staken mensen hier turf, met: For centuries people cut peat here, two men at a time: one in the pit, one loading the peat onto the cart. Light top peat was for kindling, black peat was the best fuel, reed peat was for trade. What remained, with its fens, has been De Groote Peel National Park since 1993. The walks start at the De Pelen visitor centre; a steel column remembers the aircrews who died here in the war.
Ospel heeft ruim vierduizend inwoners. S: Ospel has just over four thousand inhabitants. Since 1986 the first weekend of May brings the Moulin Blues festival, now on the grounds at the Stenenbrug, made by more than five hundred volunteers; B.B. King and Buddy Guy have played there. End of the tour.
In de Franse tijd liet Napoleon een kana: In the French era Napoleon had a canal dug from the Scheldt to the Meuse and the Rhine, the Grand Canal du Nord. When Holland was annexed by France in 1810 it was no longer needed: the work stopped and thousands of labourers lost their jobs before the canal was deep enough. Only around 1853 was the Noordervaart dug to depth, to drain the Peel and carry out the peat.
Ospel ligt op hoge, zandige grond die al: Ospel lies on high, sandy ground that reached into the Peel marshes like a peninsula. In 1840 Ospel was still a hamlet of 176 people.
